description: 👽 Terraform Orchestration Tool for DevOps. Keep environment configuration DRY with hierarchical imports of configurations, inheritance, and WAY more. Native support for Terraform and Helmfile.

summary.one_liner: Atmos is an open-source Go CLI that orchestrates Terraform, OpenTofu, Helmfile, Kubernetes, and containers across environments using stacks, components, and DRY configuration.
summary.what_it_does: Atmos lets you model infrastructure as stacks and components defined in YAML, then run the same commands locally, in CI, and through AI agents. It supports Terraform, OpenTofu, Helmfile, Kubernetes, Helm, and containers, with dependency-ordered plan and apply across components. Configuration is kept DRY through imports and inheritance, and the README describes built-in auth across AWS, Azure, and GCP, secrets from multiple backends, vendoring, a build cache, and toolchain auto-install. It also covers custom commands, workflows, hooks, stores, OPA/Rego and JSON Schema validation, and an MCP server. Git-aware change detection plans or applies only affected components in CI.
use_cases: Manage multi-account cloud environments from one config
Deploy the same Terraform code across regions and stages
Run Terraform and Helmfile releases in CI with change detection
Onboard SaaS tenants from a shared baseline configuration
Enforce compliance guardrails with OPA policies
Share vetted infrastructure configurations across teams
notable: Hierarchical stack configuration with imports and inheritance for DRY environments
Git-aware detection of affected components to limit CI work
Built-in auth, secrets masking, vendoring, and toolchain install verified by checksum
Custom commands and workflows wrap scripts as first-class atmos commands
MCP server and portable agent skills for AI tools
caveats: README does not state a paid tier, but it mentions Atmos Pro as a subscription offering for some telemetry and support features
Telemetry is collected by default and must be opted out of via atmos.yaml or an environment variable
